# Native HFS growth and shadow replay references

These committed references answer two questions: what does Apple change when an
HFS catalog grows, and can native image storage replay the acknowledged writes?
They are independent observations, not expected values generated by the Go reader.

Each macOS 15/26/27 directory retains 16 matched filesystem controls and seven
unmounted sector probes. Fresh Apple-formatted and Go-built HFS+/HFSX sources
receive the same native workload through direct raw writes and UDRO shadows.
The sector probes use blank Apple-converted images without mounting a filesystem.

- `manifest.json`: readable producer, checker verdicts, catalog growth and omitted
  read-only sector offsets; the full evidence archive is bound by SHA-256.
- `references.json.gz`: complete observations, archive hashes, native checker
  output, device geometry, metadata, file contents, resource forks and provenance.
- `native-capture.json.gz`: unchanged original capture manifest. Replay verifies
  that archive sharing changed only filenames, preserving all native values.
- `*.raw.gz`, `*.dmg.gz`, `*.shadow.gz`: complete native disks, original image
  envelopes and actual shadows, including the failing states and unused sectors.
- `commands.json` and `*.py`: exact native command transcript and hashed historical
  recipes. Go tests read this evidence; they never execute these recipes.

The 10,936,320-byte shadow controls record failed native checker verdicts, while
the matched direct writes succeed. Tail-sector writes exist in the shadow but
read-only reattachment omits them. The captured arm64 VMs use 16 KiB pages;
page-aligned probes succeed. This isolates the observed failure below HFS without
claiming the private DiskImages implementation or a universal OS-version rule.
These failures are diagnostic evidence, never passing output qualification.

Run from the repository root on Linux, Windows or macOS without mounting:

```sh
go test -count=1 -run TestNativeHFSCatalogGrowth ./acceptance
```

The corpus comes from [GitHub capture 38127438693](https://github.com/deploymenttheory/go-apfs-v3/actions/runs/38127438693).
Fresh CI captures are also replayed on all three platforms. The file-only
retention tool refuses existing destinations and validates both compressed and
decoded hashes before publishing a new index. Changes to this baseline require
new native evidence and review; ordinary test execution never refreshes it.

See [the investigation](../../../docs/hfs-header-growth.md) for the matched
controls, source-backed formatter corrections and limits of the findings. Native
operations belong on disposable CI VMs. Do not attach these images on the working
Mac.
